title.narrative: Strengthening national implementation of global biodiversity targets - NBSAP support through GIZ

description.narrative:
This project supports developing countries in improving and implementing their national biodiversity strategies and action plans (NBSAPs). NBSAPs are the key instrument for the national implementation of the Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) under the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD). The project primarily addresses intermediaries in selected partner countries, in particular decision-makers who play a role for the conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity and the restoration of ecosystems in environmental, sectoral, financial and planning authorities, the private sector, the financial sector and civil society organisations. A particular focus will be placed on representative organisations of indigenous peoples and local communities, as well as women. BMZ, GIZ and Norad has focus on gender, and climate mitigation and adaptation in this project (Riomarker 1, significant, for all 3 areas).
The partner countries selected are: Peru, Colombia, Brazil, Madagascar, Namibia, and Laos. The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Indonesia is also considered to be included the project.
